title: DNS Is Correct, and app-1 Still Calls the Wrong Server
symptom: The app on app-1 times out calling api.shop.example. The API team's dashboards are green and other servers call it fine. Someone already ran dig on app-1, and it returns the API's correct address, so they've ruled out DNS.

goals.description: app-1 resolves api.shop.example to the real API

question.prompt: Why did dig give the right answer while the app used the wrong one?
options: dig asks the DNS server directly, but programs resolve through nsswitch ('files dns'), which reads /etc/hosts first, and a leftover entry there pinned the API to its old address

debrief: dig was telling the truth about DNS, and DNS wasn't what the app used first. Programs resolve names through the C library, which follows /etc/nsswitch.conf: 'hosts: files dns' means /etc/hosts wins whenever it has an entry. 'getent hosts' resolves the same way the app does and returned 10.0.2.40, the API's old address from a migration in March, pinned 'temporarily' with a comment. Deleting the line fixes it. Two lessons: test name resolution with getent (or the app's own tooling), not only dig, when the question is 'what does this program connect to?'; and a temporary /etc/hosts pin needs an owner and an expiry, or it becomes an outage months later when the old address is reused or retired.
